analysis:
This PR is documentation and benchmark-evidence only. It adds a README index entry and a startup-shape-warmup TTFT harness (first_ttft.py, hi.py, job.sh, make_bundle.sh, run_arms.sh, session.sh, prompt.txt). No provider, coordinator, attestation, crypto or App Attest source is changed. The coordinator-to-provider WebSocket, App Attest authorization, legacy attestation paths, key handling and cache-storage threat entries (TB-002, TB-011, T-041 and others) are not touched.

Harness behavior I checked:
- The scripts run `darkbloom start --local` on loopback 127.0.0.1 with a local API key. The key is retrieved via `darkbloom local --json` and sent in a Bearer header to loopback only; it is not written to disk or logged.
- session.sh isolates provider state under a mktemp -d directory (PID, state, watchdog and kv-guard files), disables the prefix cache, and refuses to run if the port is busy or another darkbloom start/benchmark is running. It does not touch ~/.darkbloom.
- The prompts are synthetic random words with a nonce. Request text is truncated to 160 chars in output, so no consumer plaintext (A-001) is involved.
- make_bundle.sh builds an unsigned throwaway .app with a custom CFBundleIdentifier. It exists only to get a fresh per-app Metal shader cache for measurement. It does not register with a coordinator, is not a release artifact, and does not affect the binary hash registry (A-011) or qualification (A-017).
- Hardcoded absolute paths (/Users/gaj/ttft-bench) are specific to the benchmark host. They are not a vulnerability, and the scripts' shell variable usage is on trusted operator-controlled inputs.

I found no new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption. The scripts are not wired into any build or deployment pipeline in the supplied evidence. The warmup feature itself (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP) lives in code outside this batch, so any security effect of that feature, such as shape-dependent timing or cache behavior, is not reviewed here.
